newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM seeks time for new finmin to do job well.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM seeks time for new finmin to do job well.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Sunday that his new finance minister should be given time to do his job properly with the national economy in crisis.
He said he had confidence that Thanong Bidaya, a low-profile banker, would be able to handle the job effectively.
Thanong was named on Friday to replace Amnuay Viravan who quit after differences with his political rivals in the premier's six-party coalition government.
"Thanong is new in the job and we should give him enough time to study and do his job," he told a news conference.

Some analysts have said that the little-known new minister, who was president of Thai Military Bank, may not have the expertise that the respected Amnuay had with his 30-year career as banker, civil servant and politician.
Chavalit also said that he would remain in overall charge of the economy while Thanong took care of the finance ministry.
"I myself will look after the economy," he said.
Thailand is going through its worst economic slump in more than a decade with growth expected officially to fall to 5.9 percent from 6.4 percent in 1996.

The ailing finance sector is faced with loans overexposure to the depressed property sector, exports have turned sluggish, the stock market is at eight-year lows and the baht has come under speculative attack.

Amnuay's departure at this critical time for the country was viewed as negative because he had planned certain initiatives to pull Thailand out of the rut, including steep budget cuts and state-financed rescue plans for ailing financial institutions.

Chavalit said there was no need to postpone a parlimentary debate set for June 25 on the government's proposed 1997/1998 (October/September) budget next week amid a belief that the new finance minister may not be prepared to handle it.
"A man like Thanong has enough expertise and should not have problems. Some have asked me to postpone this debate on the bill but there is no need for this," he said.

Next year's proposed austerity budget of 982 billion baht ($39.3 billion), after planned cuts, represents just a four percent increase from estimated 1996/97 government spending of 944 billion baht, the smallest year-on-year growth in more than a decade.
Chavalit has said that he would continue to pursue economic policies laid down by Amnuay to beat economic woes. Thanong has pledged to do the same.
The premier said that despite Amnuay's departure, the coalition administration was united.
"My cabinet has come in to serve...we work as a team and there is no pressure. Nobody can pressure me not even elephants," he added.
